<!-- Generated by `just docs` from the code. Do not edit by hand. -->

simstim reads two files from `~/.config/simstim/` (or `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/simstim/`). `simstim config path` prints where they are, and `simstim config check` checks both files for mistakes.

## config.toml

Your preferences. Every key is optional; a missing key takes its default.

| Key | Type | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ui.motion` | string | `"auto"` | Turns the launcher's animation on or off: "auto" (off inside SSH sessions, Emacs and JetBrains terminals, and with NO_COLOR or TERM=dumb), "on" or "off". |
| `attach.detach_key` | string | `"ctrl+\"` | Leaves the session and keeps it running. Press it twice to send it to the agent. |
| `attach.image_paste_key` | string | `"ctrl+v"` | Uploads the image on the clipboard to the host and pastes its path. Without an image, the key goes to the agent. |
| `attach.scrollback` | string | `"keep"` | Says what happens to the terminal's scrollback when you attach again: "keep" replays what you missed after what you saw, "clear" starts from a clean screen. |
| `agents.inline` | boolean | `false` | Starts each agent that has one in its inline mode, where it draws in the terminal's normal screen, so your terminal keeps its scrollback: Claude Code's classic renderer, Codex with --no-alt-screen. Off by default, so each agent starts as its own defaults say. `new --inline` does it for one session. |
| `sessions.memory_max` | string | `"auto"` | Caps the memory of each new session, with everything it starts. "auto" gives the host's default: its memory minus a reserve for the system. A size is a number and a unit in powers of 1024, such as "512M", "4G", "4GiB" or "1.5G", from 256M. A host lowers a size above its limit for all sessions together to that limit. `new --memory-max` sets it for one session. |
| `sandbox.paste` | string | `"images-and-pdf"` | Sets which file types image paste and drag-and-drop may upload into a walled session: "images-and-pdf" (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP and PDF only, the default) or "any". The paste guard still refuses private files and clipboard-written paths in either mode. |
| `sandbox.package_managers` | string | `"guarded"` | Controls the settings that guest init writes for package managers inside a sandbox: "guarded" (minimum release age, no dependency install scripts for npm, pnpm, Yarn and Bun, and Go proxy settings), "strict" (also blocks pip and uv source builds), or "off". |
| `sandbox.cpus` | integer | — | Caps the CPU quota of each new session through systemd (100% per CPU). 0 uses the agent's default on walled sessions and leaves unwalled sessions unbounded. `new --cpus` overrides it. |
| `sandbox.memory` | string | — | Caps the memory of each new session, such as "4G" or "auto". `new --memory` overrides it. |
| `sandbox.disk_max` | string | — | Sets the soft disk cap for a walled session's folder, such as "10G". The supervisor stops a session past this cap with disk_full. |
| `sandbox.env` | table | — | Sets non-secret environment variables for each new session, replacing guest init defaults for those names. A name listed in [secrets] is refused with env_is_secret. `new --env` and `--env-file` override it. |
| `sandbox.keep_caches` | boolean | `true` | Keeps package and build caches across starts of a sandbox, inside that sandbox only. |
| `sandbox.caches` | array of string | — | Adds relative paths under /home/agent, or drops one with "!". |
| `sandbox.copy_in` | array of string | — | Lists laptop paths (or laptop:guest pairs) copied into each new session at start over SFTP. Paths under your home land under /home/agent; other paths land under /mnt/<name>. `new --copy` adds more. |
| `sandbox.copy_max` | string | `"64M"` | Caps the total bytes copied by copy_in and --copy at one start (default "64M"). |
| `sandbox.seed_max` | string | `"512M"` | Caps the size of each git bundle created by --seed (default "512M"). |
| `network.min_release_age` | string | `"7d"` | Sets the minimum release age for package managers inside a sandbox, as a whole number of days from "0d" to "365d". "0d" turns the age check off. |
| `network.model_budget` | integer | — | Caps the total model tokens a walled session may use across gateway requests. 0 turns the cap off. |
| `network.upload_budget` | string | `"16M"` | Caps bytes uploaded per host per hour from a walled session to non-model hosts, such as "16M". "0" turns the cap off. |
| `images.fetch` | string | `"auto"` | Sets how runtime files and images reach a host: "auto" (the host downloads from the release when reachable, falling back to a copy from this laptop), "host" (host downloads only) or "laptop" (always copied from this laptop). |
| `keymap` | table | — | Rebinds launcher commands by name ("session: delete"). A value is a key, a list of keys, or "" to unbind. `config keymap` lists the names. |
| `secrets` | table | — | Names secrets for sessions, each as a command string or a [secrets.NAME] table with run (the command that prints the value) and optional hosts, header, format and route bindings. In a walled session, secrets whose hosts come from [secrets.NAME] or the agent table stay in the egress process and never enter the sandbox. Values are never stored. |

## hosts.toml

The hosts you added. `host add` writes it, and you can edit it by hand. Each host is a `[[host]]` table.

| Key | Type | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | string | Names the host in commands, as in `attach <name>/<session>`. |
| `ssh` | string | Says how to reach the host: a Host alias from your SSH config, or user@host[:port]. |
| `ssh_config` | string | Adds an SSH config file to read as well, for example a repo's own. |
| `labels` | table | Tags the host with key-value pairs of your own, for example provider = "gcp". |
| `[provider]` | table | Names a script that starts and stops the host. Optional. |
| `provider.script` | string | Names a program that starts, stops and reports on the host. It gets the action as its argument and a JSON job on stdin (see examples/providers). |
| `provider.wake_on_attach` | boolean | Starts the host through the script when it does not answer and you attach or start a session. |
| `[machine]` | table | Records the VM, container or sandbox that `host create` made for this host. Hosts you added yourself have none. |
| `machine.provider` | string | Names the provider that made the machine: "lima", "docker" or "e2b". |
| `machine.id` | string | Names the machine as the provider knows it: the Lima instance, the Docker container, or the E2B sandbox ID. |
| `machine.user` | string | Runs the helper and the sessions on docker and e2b hosts. Lima hosts use the user from Lima's SSH config. |
| `machine.image` | string | Names the container image a docker host was made from. |
| `machine.template` | string | Names the E2B template a sandbox was made from. It sets the sandbox's CPUs and memory. |
| `machine.idle_stop` | string | Sets how long the host may go with no client connected and no session working before it stops: a duration such as "30m", or "never". A Lima VM powers itself off (30m by default; it needs passwordless sudo). An E2B sandbox pauses when its lease runs out (15m by default). |
| `machine.autostart` | string | Says when a local Lima VM on macOS starts by itself through `limactl autostart`: "boot" (at system boot), "login" (when you log in), or empty (off). |
| `machine.busy_lease` | string | Sets how long an E2B sandbox keeps running after the last client goes, while a session is working (60m by default). |
| `machine.token_command` | string | Prints the E2B API key, for example a read from your keychain. It is used when E2B_API_KEY is not set and the E2B CLI is not logged in. The key is never written down. |
| `machine.stdin` | string | Says how keys reach an E2B sandbox: "send" (one request for each chunk, the default) or "stream" (one long request; not yet proved on E2B's servers). |
| `machine.created` | string | Records when `host create` made this machine (RFC3339Nano UTC), so two machines of the same host and provider ID can be told apart. |
| `secrets` | array of string | Lists secrets from config.toml that every new session on this host gets, for example ["ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"]. `new --secret` adds more. |
| `wall_floor` | string | Is the weakest sandbox level that new sessions on this host may get: "none", "process", "gvisor" or "microvm". |
| `trusted` | boolean | Marks a host where you control root. Untrusted hosts default to false and do not receive secrets unless explicitly allowed. |
| `[sandbox]` | table | Holds per-host defaults for session sizes, environment variables, laptop copies and kept caches. Host settings win over config.toml's [sandbox] table, and command-line flags win over both. |
| `sandbox.cpus` | integer | Caps the CPU quota of new sessions on this host. |
| `sandbox.memory` | string | Caps the memory of new sessions on this host, such as "4G". |
| `sandbox.disk_max` | string | Sets the soft disk cap for walled sessions on this host, such as "10G". |
| `sandbox.env` | table | Sets non-secret environment variables for new sessions on this host. |
| `sandbox.copy_in` | array of string | Lists laptop paths (or laptop:guest pairs) copied into new sessions on this host at start. |
| `sandbox.keep_caches` | boolean | Overrides sandbox.keep_caches from config.toml for this host. |
| `sandbox.caches` | array of string | Adds relative cache paths under /home/agent, or drops one with a leading "!", layered on top of sandbox.caches from config.toml. |
